correctness.rationale: Direct compression of the three-state Fourier propagator yields the stated K matrix; simple-eigenvalue perturbation away from fixed sampling revivals gives a squared-eigenvalue-modulus deficit of nine-halves times the squared observation interval and squared phase; degenerate first-order diagonalization at full sampling revivals gives two squared-eigenvalue-modulus deficits with leading coefficient the squared observation interval. The eigenprojectors are uniformly bounded and become orthogonal at revival, yielding the full survival limit and uniform exponential survival-tail bound, hence all moment limits. The exact full-Hamiltonian reconstructions, Lyapunov means and survival comparisons in verify.py passed 49 checks. Numerical checks are ancillary, not proof.
